correctness.rationale: For any maximal bottom-fibre point s, each of the m incomparable middle targets must be represented on a distinct immediate Boolean successor, so n-|s|>=m. At n=m all n atoms have different middle colours; at n=m+1 the bottom fibre is empty plus some singleton worlds. A fixed z>=1 of these forces a bijective assignment of middle colours to covers at each zero singleton, equivalent to a proper edge-colouring of K_z with the remaining z-1 colours. Only z=1 or even z can occur. All higher-rank colours are forced by monotonicity; the converse assignments satisfy back-lifting for each middle target. The disjoint cases yield the displayed formula. Direct independent enumeration of all monotone maps/back lifts confirms 2,30,162 for (n,m)=(2,2),(3,2),(4,3), while exact colouring enumeration confirms F_2=1,F_4=6,F_6=720. These are corroborative finite checks, not a proof of the general bijection.
